calls.title: Sam's four Accounting codes filed under Business
calls.text: On 2026-11-24 Sam's saves filed the local codes ACC, ACCT, ACCTG and ACTG under Business. The Accounting re-point dry run moves 907 courses under 372 M-IDs to ACCT under Accounting; its apply waits until those four are refiled under Accounting, or Sam says to go ahead over them. Copper Mountain's ACC is ACCESS, disability services, and stays out, keyed by college.
calls.if_no_reply: Nothing is re-minted; the courses stay under Business and the dry run stands.
calls.link_text: The Accounting re-point dry run, PR 3867

calls.title: The noncredit subject title list
calls.text: The list holds 129 headings from the four large noncredit programs as 114 titles. Sam settles which headings join one title, and whether Citizenship, Health and Safety, substantial disabilities and Workforce Preparation take a common code or none.
calls.if_no_reply: The noncredit hold stands and the list stays a draft.

answer.words: "Looks good. Based on a quick check on my phone. Can we go with it and I can look more closely tomorrow and reverse or change anything that looks wrong?" (in session, about 03:50Z). The 114 titles stand and the hold is lifted (#3667); the five categories with no common code keep none (r-noncredit-title-list-go-sam-2026-11-22). He may change the list after a closer look.

calls.title: Aligning 192 Cerritos courses whose M-ID sits under another Common SUBJ
calls.text: Sam's saved subject decisions put 192 Cerritos courses under a Common SUBJ other than the one their M-ID was minted under; ATH's 84 sit under ATHL against his KINE, and on ordinary titles the decided code and the M-ID agree for 253 of 440. Aligning them is a re-mint under the re-mint playbook, with its dry run and alias map.
calls.if_no_reply: Nothing is re-minted; the courses keep their M-IDs and the page shows the decided code beside them.

answer.words: I'm thinking it would be best to finish the common subject and local subject titles before reminting MIDs.

calls.title: Two forestry courses still sit on AGRI under a parent on ENVR
calls.text: Open Asks Sheet 105 card 1: AGRI M10SY Forest Surveying and AGRI M1104 Introduction to Forest Operations are merged into Forest Ecology, which moved to ENVR on Sheet 104. The dry run that moves both to ENVR is committed; the session's permission check held its apply.
calls.no_reply: Both stay on AGRI, merged into an ENVR parent; nothing else waits on the card.

answer.words: move-both (Open Asks Sheet 107 card 1; applied by S436, kb/forestry_wine_remint_out/2026-10-20-stragglers/)

calls.title: Six curated anchor entries the re-key dry run cannot settle
calls.text: Three collide with other courses on their new Common SUBJ and need fresh numbers; three hospitality entries have no MQ discipline. On no reply they stay unapplied.

next_step.title: Fold Cerro Coso's and Porterville's glued letter into the course number
next_step.text: COCI stores some Cerro Coso courses as PHEDC 103 where the college prints PHED C103, and Porterville's the same with P. Fold those state-only codes in the COCI lookup builder for the two colleges only, dry run first measuring every consumer, then rebuild the subject family.

changes.text: The Subjects tab lists all 118 colleges by title source, with a status for each way to look and the next step.
The course panel folds each group, carries a move row with a subject picker at the top of each group, and lists credit codes before noncredit.
Every MQ discipline in the 20th-edition handbook has a common subject code: 95 assigned, each with a confidence; Flight Attendant Training is FLTR on Sam's pick.
The Subjects panel opens beside the view, never over it.

The subject map leaves AED unmapped: Cerritos's Adult Education is a mixed noncredit bucket, and its Electricity entry gave 45 shared M-IDs an ELEC prefix. Nothing re-mints until the scope's codes are settled.
The four noncredit MQ disciplines take common codes: Citizenship CTZN, Health and Safety HLSN, Home Economics HMEN, DSPS Noncredit DSPN. Only Workforce Preparation keeps no code.
Exhibits with no credit recommendation go on the MAP Team Queue tab as a worklist.

Sam's four asks: Cerritos's department list titles its codes (AED Adult Education, STAT Statistics) and a decision carries a source link; the panel resizes and keeps its top row frozen; a course or a group moves to another common subject code from the panel; every Subjects table sorts and resizes (#3687).

Settle a code at every college: one common subject code and one Save write a kb_curation row per college at its credit form's key, under the reviewer's own email; a college a person or filing settled keeps it, a noncredit-only code keeps its category forms (#3687).

Edit on every code row and the course panel over every Subjects surface; every count opens the rows it counts; the surfaces take the window's width; Local titles reads 88 of 101 codes at Los Angeles Pierce

Noncredit codes get a save per COCI noncredit category, keyed SUBJ:college|code|nc:category; 275 codes get a noncredit form, 64 span several categories, 37 have no category on file; a form with no title field writes no title, and a title saved before its category moved shows read-only (#3671).

The daily build reads saved subject decisions: a college's save, then a statewide List filing, then the subject map, then a recommendation; codes with a common code rose from 888 to 918. Shell titles such as work experience stay held, and the mint plan equals main's (#3670).
Santa Ana's and Mt. San Antonio's credit catalogs are filed with their headings; Not read yet fell from 388 to 156 and titled codes rose from 1,412 to 1,636 (#3669).

The noncredit hold is lifted on Sam's word: the noncredit title list no longer reads as a draft, the 54 held rows became ordinary rows, and noncredit and noncredit enhanced courses show apart (#3667).
Sam's 30 Cerritos subject decisions are filed in kb_curation under cohort subjects-s701@bot, with a receipt and a rollback beside it.
Edit and Save on the Subjects page: a signed-in reviewer saves a local title or common code as one kb_curation row, and Take it back removes only that reviewer's own save (#3666).

Three large noncredit catalogs are filed (San Diego College of Continuing Education, Santa Ana School of Continuing Education, Mt. San Antonio noncredit), and a draft noncredit subject title list opens inside Subjects; the list opens on All subjects with a Credit and Noncredit filter, and ATH is KINE (#3662).
A local code opens that college's courses in a side panel, credit and noncredit apart, each with its C-ID, CCN and M-ID (#3661).

The 21 subject pages the catalog indexes link are read and filed (493 courses), and each row with no title shows a recommended local title or common code with its measured level; 108 web searches are filed for the Not in catalog rows (#3660).
The held view, opened from a figure on the Subjects card, lists the local subject codes the pile mint holds on: 1,341 courses, 416 codes, 678 college-and-code pairs.
Both Subjects files rebuild in the daily build when their content changes; a failed step keeps yesterday's file and the publish goes on.

The Subjects card on the Commons front reads 16 colleges, 1,431 college-and-code pairs and 746 printed names; 753 of 1,625 codes get a common subject code from the existing files. Its builder is not in the daily build yet.
Curation step b, the local subject title, has an owner: the Courses bot drafts each title and a curator settles the ones that disagree. Sam left the call to the session on Nov 20.

The anchor re-key applied: 20 curated anchor entries onto their Common SUBJ, 15 keeping their number and 5 on the lowest free number of DIES or PARA; the three hospitality entries stay with the curator (#2938).
The anchor re-key dry run reads the anchor's era from its keys and applies only later maps: 2 re-keys, 15 prefix swaps, 6 for Sam (#2935).
A recorded note settles a weak mnemonic, and the anchor findings are their own re-key item, so nothing waits on a curator (#2857).
Saves read the sign-in at write time, and a lapsed sign-in says so
A row press edits the row and moves the panel; Check alignment audits a typed code
Estimating's common subject code reads ESTG everywhere; ESTI is a local Esthetics code at four colleges.
The college table counts the codes that need attention, the panel leads with ways to act, and course lines read with their subject code.
The Subjects card carries quick links under its headline and opens with its sections folded.
A code the catalog index leaves out is read at its own address: Cerritos INST is Interdisciplinary Studies, Long Beach City CART is Creative Arts.
The pages eleven web searches found were read; none names its code, so each is recorded as tried.
The Subjects card matches a college's name as the table does, so a save at Los Angeles Trade-Technical lifts its codes on the card too.

Every untitled code with no filed web search now has one: 205 searched, 6 more codes carry a recommended title, and the 69 pages the searches found were read; none names its code, so each is recorded as tried.
The quarterly MQ compare reads against the 20th edition; the runner read the same edition and hash.

The MQ disciplines view opens from the Subjects card: each discipline's list type, provisions, common code and what to look at; a code opens the statewide list filtered to it, and a count opens a second sidebar beside the first.
A Courses count in the MQ view or the statewide list opens its code's own small course file instead of the 17 MB state course list.

The codes with no title became Titles to check: a title COBI rates 80 or more stands as a derived title with its confidence bar, and about 100 of the 301 codes remain, each with Accept on the row and beside every candidate title.

Confidence shows as one 0 to 100 bar; a web search on the college's own site counts as a candidate, so Clovis MECH reads Mechatronics/Industrial Automation; a sidebar resize leaves 360 pixels of the view.
A list of 8,786 college and local subject codes with no title went to COBIx, each with a recommended title and its measured confidence; Sam ruled that no M-ID is minted on a local code.
Runners read every college's catalog subject index: the Subjects record names 8,147 local subject codes at 103 colleges, up from 1,655 at 19.
COBIx's leftover local subject titles filed: 911 titles at 18 colleges, each with its source; 96 department labels kept as hints (PR 3841).
The stray-code re-mint as a dry run: the in-scope M-IDs retire and their courses return to Needs an M-ID (PR 3843).
The stray-code rescore scored 0 to 100 in place of levels; the dry run takes 90 or more: 66 local subjects, 92 M-IDs retire, 48 held (PR 3846).
The Local subjects view opens a sidebar of a code's courses; a reviewer moves one or several to another common subject (PR 3851).
The stray-code re-mint applied: 60 M-IDs retired, 20 merged shells aliased, 35 held; Needs an M-ID 1,819 to 1,881 (PR 3853).
Local subject recommendations score 0 to 100 and the Subjects panel draws the confidence bar (PR 3859).
The Accounting re-point dry run: 372 M-IDs and 907 courses move to ACCT under Accounting, 1 held, 29 families flagged; the apply waits on Sam's four Business filings (PR 3867).
The lightning round takes Not a subject, Skip for the visit, the example course's description, the catalog link in a bottom bar, a folded How this works and a training note (PR 3893).
LACCD's class search titles 171 of 212 untitled codes at the district's nine colleges; 87 differ from the catalog, and the catalog stands (PR 3894).
